title: The end of an era #phantomoftheopera #broadway #theatre
transcript: I'm not gonna lie, the fandom closing is hitting me a little hard today. And. And I tweeted this out, and I stand by this. But the reason why I think that shows should close after 10 years is because when shows stay open on Broadway forever, they very rarely release the rights to regional productions, and so you rarely get other people's visions of a work. We've only had 2 versions of The Phantom of the opera in the last 35 years in the US. I guess 3 if you count the Vegas version. We have had so many versions of into the Woods in that same amount of time. And so it's just about, like, letting pieces grow and evolve beyond what they were originally. But the reason that I feel like this is hitting me so hard today is because of the things that we are going to lose from losing Phantom on Broadway. We are losing Maria bjornson's designs, and she died in 2002. But her scenic and costume design for Phantom were historical. We lost how Prince in 2019. This was the last show on Broadway that he directed. Composers get cast recordings, playwrights get published, but directors and designers, their work is ephemeral. It's. It's out there, and then it's gone. Unless works of art get recorded. And, of course, there's always archival recordings. But we don't have a pro shot of a fully stage Phantom. We just have the concert versions, and that's A little heartbreaking to me. And of course, we have the costumes, um, that are going to be on display. There's. There's been costumes on display at the museum of Broadway. Um, but there's just something about losing that production. And we always lose that, but especially when it's artists that we've lost. It feels like losing them all over again. That's a little heartbreaking.
